overall_summary: Deduplication of the hourly observation records reveals 28 unique videos. Performance heavily skews toward space and planetary anomaly content published within late September and early October 2026. Specifically, 'What If' speculative scenarios and extreme planetary attributes (e.g., Venus day length, liquid diamond planets, burning ice, dark planets) generate the highest views-per-day and engagement metrics (likes/comments per view). Conversely, psychological tricks, mundane animal facts, and older September content show flat or negligible recent velocity.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (IYuce8vaU3Y) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (8KEl0_pJ_68) achieved over 970 to 1,029 views quickly with high engagement ratios (up to 38 likes).
winning_patterns.action: Double down on high-stakes, physics-bending 'What If' scenarios involving extreme cosmic bodies.

winning_patterns.evidence: Titles featuring impossible-sounding facts like 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (A9Qa-RmuOr0) and 'The Planet Darker Than Coal' (v1rrcZLdp4U) drove over 980 to 1,032 views with robust like counts.
winning_patterns.action: Continue sourcing bizarre, counter-intuitive real-world space facts that immediately challenge common assumptions.

weak_patterns.evidence: Videos focusing on standard animal trivia (e.g., 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts', 'The Only Animal That Can Live Forever') garnered lower velocity and sparse engagement outside of isolated outliers.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize standard standalone animal facts unless framed within a high-stakes cinematic survival or extreme mystery context.

weak_patterns.evidence: Content regarding psychological tricks (e.g., 'The Psychological Trick to Stop Songs Stuck in Your Head') generated minimal traction (71 views) compared to cosmic phenomena.
weak_patterns.action: Pause standard self-help or basic psychology tips to focus resources on top-performing space and mystery niches.
